corpusSummary: The corpus surveys social-science studies of large language models across behavior, interaction, health, education, and policy. It highlights LLM-based modeling of social dynamics, human–AI trust and embodiment, AI as a research instrument with governance concerns, and AI-enabled learning and assessment. Across these domains, findings stress reliability, ethical equity, transparency, and the need for human oversight.

themes.name: LLM-driven social dynamics
themes.description: LLMs are used to model and analyze social dynamics, including opinion formation, polarization, and multi-agent interactions, with critical attention to biases and validity.

themes.name: Human–AI interaction, trust, embodiment, and well-being
themes.description: A broad research thread investigates how people trust, relate to, and are affected by AI in everyday contexts—health, education, consumer tech—and how design features shape outcomes.

themes.name: AI as research instrument and governance
themes.description: Researchers explore LLMs as research tools for analysis, data extraction, and knowledge discovery, while developing governance frameworks and validation standards.

themes.name: AI in education and learning
themes.description: Studies examine AI tutoring, scaffolding, assessment, and literacy, and their effects on learning, motivation, and pedagogy.

emergingKeywords: validation and transparency in AI research
